Pramod Nair([[Chief financial officer|CFO]]) | industry = [[Building material]]s | products = | revenue = {{increase}} {{INRConvert|1685.46|c}}{{cite web | url=https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/55afc78c-2323-4c64-a5f1-31349a7d4bd3.pdf| title=Everest Industries Limited|work=BSE India}} | revenue_year = 2023 | operating_income = {{up}} {{INRConvert|1645|c}} | income_year = 2023 | assets = {{increase}}{{INRConvert|1133.35|c}} | assets_year = 2023 | num_employees = 1400+ (2024) | subsidiaries = {{plainlist| *Everest Buildpro Private Limited *Everest Steel Building Private Limited *Everest Building Products *Everestind FZE}} | website = {{URL|https://www.everestind.com/}} }} '''Everest Industries Limited''', is an Indian company that manufactures building materials.{{cite web |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/everest-inds-to-set-up-manufacturing-facility-in-south-india-123022100842_1.html|title=Everest Inds to set up manufacturing facility in South India|work=Business Standard|access-date=28 May 2024}} It has a presence in around 35 countries and employs around 1400 employees. Everest Industries operates these business segments: roofing, ceiling, wall, flooring, cladding solutions, pre-engineered steel buildings and other building materials.{{cite web |url=https://realty.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/allied-industries/building-solutions-firm-everest-industries-plans-rs-60-crore-expansion-in-nashik/52985768 |title=Building solutions firm Everest Industries plans Rs 60 crore expansion in Nashik|work=Economic times|access-date=12 May 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.zeebiz.com/market-news/news-money-making-opportunity-in-chat-with-anil-singhvi-sandeep-jain-recommends-everest-industries-as-a-stock-to-buy-149848|title=Money-making opportunity! In chat with Anil Singhvi, Sandeep Jain recommends Everest Industries as a stock to buy|work=Zee Business|date=17 February 2021 |access-date=28 May 2024}} ==History== Everest Industries Limited was founded in 1934 under the name of Asbestos Cement Ltd.{{cite web |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/photos/business/personal-finance/born-before-indias-independence-these-companies-grew-to-be-mf-favourites-heres-their-journey-9024011-15.html |title=Born before India's independence, these companies grew to be MF favourites. Here's their journey |work=Money Control|access-date=12 May 2024}} in [[Maharashtra]]. In 1983, the company changed its name to Everest Building Product Ltd., in the same year the company went public on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]].{{cite web |url=https://www.bseindia.com/stock-share-price/everest-industries-ltd/everestind/508906/corp-information/ |title=Everest Industries Ltd |work=BSE India|access-date=12 May 2024}} In 1990 the company was renamed Eternit Everest Ltd. It got its current name in 2003. In 1995, it also got listed on the [[National Stock Exchange of India]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nseindia.com/get-quotes/equity?symbol=EVERESTIND |title=Everest Industries Limited Share Price |url=https://www.constructionweekonline.in/business/everest-industries-ltd-wins-cidc-vishwakarma-award|title=Everest Industries Ltd wins CIDC Vishwakarma Award|work=constructionweekonline|date=24 May 2010 |access-date=12 May 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.cidc.in/support/viswakarma/New/CVKA-2010-Awardees.pdf|title=List of Awardees – 2nd CIDC Vishwakarma Awards 2010|work=CIDC|access-date=12 May 2024}} In the same year it also received the ICWAI award by [[Salman Khurshid]], [[Minister of External Affairs (India)]].{{cite web |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/news-archive/web/everest-industries-bags-icwai-award-again|title=Everest Industries bags ICWAI award again|work=IndianExpress|date=12 July 2010 |access-date=12 May 2024}} ==Operations== It employs around 1400 people around the world and reached a combined revenue of INR 1685 crore in 2024.{{cite news |title=Outcome of the Board Meeting and Audited Financial 2024 |access-date=2 August 2024}} It has three manufacturing plants for pre-engineered steel buildings- Roorkee in Uttarakhand, Ranchi in Jharkhand and Dahej in Gujarat.{{cite news
